rules.statement: Don't report a check that classifies a type by its base class as a hard-coded rule needing a separate flag when deriving from that base is the documented, defining fact the rest of the design relies on.
rules.why: When the derivation is the registered fact (descriptor properties are defined by it, other validation reads it), a separate flag would only restate that fact and could contradict it.
rules.check: Before reporting, see whether the base class is what related descriptor properties or docs define the classification by, and whether an ADR or a comment at the check records it. Report only if neither does.

rules.statement: Don't ask to merge similar error-message formatting code from different packages into one shared helper when the copies format different types, or when sharing would add public API just for a message fragment.
rules.why: One formatter can't serve unrelated types. Making it public in an abstractions package to reuse an error-text fragment costs more than it saves, and tests that pin each message already catch wording drift.
rules.check: Before reporting duplicate formatting, check whether each copy formats the same type, whether they're in the same package, and whether a shared helper would have to be public. Also check whether tests pin each message's exact text.

rules.statement: Give every branch of code that builds user-visible error text a test that asserts the exact text, including edge branches such as an exact single value and an open-ended range.
rules.why: Otherwise a regression in an untested branch changes the user-visible error text without failing any test.
rules.check: When a diff adds or changes a formatter with several branches for error messages, check that tests reach each branch and assert the full text.

rules.statement: Don't give a method a bool parameter that switches what it outputs. Split it into separately named methods, or have the caller pass in the varying behavior.
rules.why: A bool flag hides its meaning at the call site.
rules.check: Look for new or changed methods whose bool parameter picks between different output formats or behaviors.

rules.statement: In a test project, create mocks from the test base's strict, verified MockRepository instead of using a loose Mock.Of, and mark expected calls .Verifiable().
rules.why: A loose mock returns null on an unexpected call instead of failing the test, so it hides unintended interactions.
rules.check: Look for Mock.Of<T>() or new Mock<T>() with default (loose) behavior in tests. Mocks should come from the base class's MockRepository(MockBehavior.Strict) and be verified on dispose.
